text: “I’ve always had a kind of idea that English girls were just a mite moss-grown. Old-fashioned and sweet, you know, but scared to move round without a footman or a maiden aunt. I guess I’m a bit behind the times!” The upshot of these confidential relations was that Tommy and Tuppence took up their abode forthwith at the Ritz, in order, as Tuppence put it, to keep in touch with Jane Finn’s only living relation. “And put like that,” she added confidentially to Tommy, “nobody could boggle at the expense!” Nobody did, which was the great thing. “And now,” said the young lady on the morning after their installation, “to work!” Mr. Beresford put down the Daily Mail, which he was reading, and applauded with somewhat unnecessary vigour.
